pk.context: 100 mg single oral dose, fasted healthy male volunteers

clues.title: Approval and strengths
clues.text: Approved by FDA in March 1998 as film-coated tablets for oral use, in 25, 50 and 100 mg strengths.

clues.title: Sponsor
clues.text: The original application was filed by Pfizer. The label is now held by Viatris.

clues.title: Class and selectivity
clues.text: A selective inhibitor of phosphodiesterase type 5. It is only about 10-fold more potent on PDE5 than on PDE6, an enzyme of the retina.

clues.title: Pathway
clues.text: Blocks breakdown of cGMP downstream of nitric oxide, prolonging smooth muscle relaxation. At recommended doses it does nothing without that nitric oxide signal.

clues.title: Drug substance
clues.text: A citrate salt of molecular weight 666.7; the free base, C₂₂H₃₀N₆O₄S, is 474.6. White to off-white crystalline powder, 3.5 mg/mL soluble in water.

clues.title: Tablet
clues.text: Blue, rounded-diamond film-coated tablets, coloured with FD&C Blue No. 2 aluminum lake. Lactose and croscarmellose sodium are among the excipients.

clues.title: Absorption and food
clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is 41%. A high-fat meal delays Tmax by about 60 minutes and lowers Cmax by 29%.

clues.title: Metabolism and excretion
clues.text: Cleared mainly by CYP3A4 (CYP2C9 minor) to an N-desmethyl metabolite with half the parent’s potency. 96% is protein bound; about 80% of a dose is excreted in feces.

clues.title: Contraindications
clues.text: Contraindicated with nitrates in any form and with guanylate cyclase stimulators such as riociguat, because hypotension is potentiated.

clues.title: Indication
clues.text: Indicated for the treatment of erectile dysfunction. Common adverse reactions are headache, flushing and dyspepsia; sudden vision loss (NAION) is a warning.
